messages:
anika: quick proposal — we need a single, deterministic fallback arbitration for canary rollouts rather than ad-hoc fallbacks across layers. thinking priority: model-variant -> region -> capacity. intent is to preserve user experience first, then locality, then cost.

Tim: +1 to deterministic priority but worried about quality regressions if we always prefer cheaper model variants. how do we detect a latent quality drop?

sara: we should gate model-variant fallback with an eval signal. if quality delta > X (e.g., eval BLEU/ROUGE or classifier p(hallucination) up), then skip model fallback and try region/capacity next.

mike: agree. also add runtime signals: p95 latency > 600ms or error_rate > 1% triggers fallback path. those are already in alerts.

anika: exactly — rollout config proposal (draft):
```yaml
rollout: 
  canary: 5%
  fallback_priority: ["model_variant","region","capacity"]
  guards:
    quality_delta_threshold: 0.05  # relative drop
    latency_p95_threshold_ms: 600
    error_rate_threshold_pct: 1.0
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  backoff_policy: exponential
```

tim: that looks sensible. couple of API questions: 1) do we expose fallback order as array or enum? 2) should customers be able to override per-route?

anika: expose as list for maximum flexibility. yes allow per-route override but we should validate overrides against account-level guardrails (security/cost limits).

sara: telemetry: we must emit a structured event whenever fallback happens with fields: route, reason_code (LATENCY/ERROR/QUALITY/CAPACITY), from_model, to_model, region_from, region_to, active_traffic_pct. otherwise debugging is a mess.

mike: add also a metric for "fallback_churn" to catch oscillations — count of fallback events per route per minute. if that spikes, we should circuit-break rollouts.

ops-bot: incident-safety-check: remember cascading fallbacks where model fallback causes spike in another region and that cascades back. propose: global in-flight cap per-route and a small randomized jitter before re-routing.

anika: good call. add randomized jitter (0-50ms) + per-route in-flight cap. also add a hard kill-switch in console to stop automatic fallbacks (manual override).

tim: UX: in console show live fallback layer, reason, and last N events. allow pinning a fallback ("pin to variant-v2") and also rolling back canary. show expected cost delta if pinned.

mike: one more edge-case: when region fallback happens due to spot preemption (capacity), we prefer regional replica in same continent, not cross-continent, to avoid latency spike — so region selection must be topology-aware.

sara: agree. we should encode region affinity in routing table and prefer nearest healthy region unless quality guard forces model fallback.

anika: I'll update the RFC with: 1) config schema, 2) telemetry/events contract, 3) console UX mocks, 4) test plan (load + quality canary), 5) safety knobs (cooldown, backoff, kill-switch).

mike: can you also add a small playbook snippet for oncall? like quick triage steps and metric checks. saves time during incidents.

anika: yep — will add.

tim: ack. volunteer to own the telemetry events contract.

sara: I'll draft the quality gating integration with evals/monitoring.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-fallbacks/rfc-draft -> staging at 1774123500.

anika: thanks — will open RFC PR and link here when ready. :thumbsup:
